scope: Synthetic AES-256-GCM cross-library and real HistoryStore record interoperability only
directions: Python cryptography AESGCM ciphertext to Rust HistoryStore records
Rust HistoryStore ciphertext to Python AESGCM decryption and record-schema comparison
Rust seal_record payload to Python AESGCM decryption

wire.aad_identifier_encoding: UTF-8, appended directly with no delimiter
wire.table: history (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, sealed BLOB NOT NULL)

limits: No OS-keychain migration or credential backend exercised.
No normal profiles, real user text, UI, observers, permission changes or dictionary changes.
HistoryRecord exposes scalar authored_spans but not authorship version; authorship:1 is checked in authenticated wire payloads.
Source/rlib/binary hashes identify supplied artifacts; this probe does not independently attest how the rlibs were built.
Private-directory isolation assumes no hostile concurrent replacement of probe paths.
observations: Only injected synthetic keys and owned private SQLite files were used.
No OS-keychain migration, normal-profile or native-authorship acceptance is established.
Standalone throwaway probes linked the actual product rlib; this is not a Rust self-roundtrip.
